title: Example
body_md:
An important class of problems falling in the domain of \eqref{eq:P} is the equilibrium selection problem 
$$
\min_{x} f_{1}(x) +g_{1}(x) \quad\text{s.t. }x\in \textnormal{SOL}({\mathsf{F}}_{2},\mathcal{K}) 
$$
where $f_{1}:\mathcal{X}\to\varmathbb{R}$ is Lipschitz smooth and $g_1:\mathcal{X}\to(-\infty,\infty]$ is a proper closed convex function, and $\mathcal{K}\subseteq\mathcal{X}$ a nonempty closed convex set. In this formulation, the composite convex function in the upper level defines a design criterion, used to select among the solution set of a variational inequality problem 
\[
\text{ Find }y\in\mathcal{K}\text{ s.t. : } \inner{{\mathsf{F}}_{2}(y),x-y}\geq 0\qquad\forall x\in\mathcal{K}.
\]
In this case, finite-sum representation on the lower level naturally appears when this VI comes from matrix games or constrained optimization reformulated as a saddle-point problem \citep{alacaoglu2022stochastic,nesterovNemirovski13acta}. 
Stochastic versions of the equilibrium selection problem have only been studied so far in \cite{jalilzadeh2024stochastic}. They develop a stochastic approximation algorithm based on the extragradient method, and show an $O(1/\varepsilon^{4})$ iteration complexity at both levels. This rate is inferior to our scheme, which can achieve $O(1/\varepsilon^{3})$ iteration complexity. 
If ${\mathsf{F}}_{2}=\nabla f_{2}$, for a convex smooth and real-valued function $f_{2}$, we recover the simple bilevel optimization problem \citep{Solodov:2007aa,Dempe:2021aa}. As far as we know, the only analysis of stochastic versions of the simple bilevel optimization problem is reported in \cite{cao2023projection}, where a stochastic Frank-Wolfe method is shown to display an $O(1/\varepsilon)$ iteration complexity.

title: Remark
body_md:
Consider the bound on $W_{\rm Feas}$, where we substitute $\bar{\tau}= \frac{\sqrt{\theta}\gamma}{L_{1}}$. Omitting numerical constants, we obtain the bound
\begin{align*}
W_{\rm Feas}(K,x_{0},x^{*},\mathcal{U}_{2})
                                             
                                     
                                                                                           
&\leq \frac{L_1\max_{x\in\mathcal{U}_{2}}\norm{x-x_{0}}^{2}+L_1\norm{x^{*}-x_{0}}^{2}}{\gamma(1-\gamma)\sqrt{\theta}K}+\frac{\bar{h}_{\rho}+ C_{\mathcal{U}_{2}} }{(1-\gamma)K^{\delta}},
\end{align*}
where we've used $\gamma,\theta\in (0,1)$ and hence $1\leq 1/(1-\gamma)$ and $1\leq 1/(\gamma \sqrt{\theta})$, as well as $1/K\leq 1/K^{\delta}$ for $K\geq 1$. Thus, to attain an $\varepsilon$-optimal solution in terms of the feasibility gap, it is sufficient to take $K=O\left(\max\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{\theta}\varepsilon},\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{1/\delta}}\right\}\right)$ iterations. Each iteration on average requires $\theta |\mathcal{A}|+2$ evaluations of ${\mathsf{V}}^{\mathtt{a}}_{k}$. Thus, to reach accuracy $\varepsilon$ on average the algorithm needs 
$O\left(\max\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{\theta}\varepsilon},\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{1/\delta}}\right\}\right) \cdot (\theta |\mathcal{A}|+2)$ evaluations of the stochastic oracle. Optimizing this estimate with respect to $\theta$ gives $\theta=2/|\mathcal{A}|$, and the total complexity becomes 
$O\left(\max\left\{\frac{\sqrt{|\mathcal{A}|}}{\varepsilon},\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{1/\delta}}\right\}\right)$. 
Note that existing (deterministic) algorithms would require $|\mathcal{A}|$ evaluations of ${\mathsf{V}}^{\mathtt{a}}_{k}$ per iteration, and the total complexity is $|\mathcal{A}|\max\{1/\varepsilon,1/\varepsilon^{1/\delta}\}$ evaluations of ${\mathsf{V}}^{\mathtt{a}}_{k}$. This demonstrates the potential effectiveness of variance reduction. We also note that each term in the maximum has a natural interpretation. The first term corresponds to the standard single-level setting and is the same as in \cite{alacaoglu2022stochastic}; The second term stems from the hierarchical tructure of our problem and indicates the intrinsic complexity of the bilevel problem.

label: lem:nemirovski
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nemirovski}
Let ${\varmathbb{F}}=(\mathcal{F}_{k})_{k\in\varmathbb{N}}$ be a filtration and $(Z_{k})_{k\in\varmathbb{N}}$ an ${\varmathbb{F}}$-adapted stochastic process with values in $\mathcal{X}$ and $\varmathbb{E}[Z_{k+1}\vert\mathcal{F}_{k}]=0$. Then, for any $K\geq 1,x_{0}\in\mathcal{X}$ and any compact set $\mathcal{C}\subset\mathcal{X}$, 
$$
\varmathbb{E}\left[\max_{x\in\mathcal{C}}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\inner{Z_{k+1},x}\right]\leq\max_{x\in\mathcal{C}}\frac{1}{2}\norm{x_{0}-x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\varmathbb{E}[\norm{Z_{k+1}}^{2}]. 
$$

label: lem:gap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gap}
    Let $\mathcal{C}\subset\operatorname{dom}(g)$  be a nonempty compact convex set. Consider problem $\operatorname{HVI}({\mathsf{F}},g)$ with ${\mathsf{F}}:\mathcal{Z}\to\mathcal{Z}$ monotone and Lipschitz continuous. The function $x\mapsto \Theta(x\vert{\mathsf{F}},g,\mathcal{C})$ is well-defined and convex on $\mathcal{Z}$. For any $x\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\Theta(x\vert {\mathsf{F}},g,\mathcal{C})\geq 0.$ Moreover, if $x\in\mathcal{C}$ is a solution to $\operatorname{HVI}({\mathsf{F}},g)$, then $\Theta(x\vert{\mathsf{F}},g,\mathcal{C})=0$. Conversely, if $\Theta(x\vert{\mathsf{F}},g,\mathcal{C})=0$ for some $x\in\mathcal{C}$ for which there exists an $\varepsilon>0$ such that $\varmathbb{B}(x,\varepsilon)\cap\mathcal{C}=\varmathbb{B}(x,\varepsilon)\cap\operatorname{dom}(g)$, then $x$ is a solution of $\operatorname{HVI}({\mathsf{F}},g)$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let ${\mathsf{F}}:\mathcal{Z}\to\mathcal{Z}$ be continuous and monotone over $\operatorname{dom}(g)\subset\mathcal{Z}$. Assume $\operatorname{dom}(g)$ is closed. The solution set $\mathcal{S}$ of $\operatorname{HVI}({\mathsf{F}},g)$ is \emph{weakly sharp} if there exists $\tau>0$ such that 
\[
(\forall z^{\ast}\in\mathcal{S}):\quad \tau\varmathbb{B}(0,1)\subseteq{\mathsf{F}}(z^{\ast})+\partial g(z^{\ast})+[\operatorname{\mathsf{TC}}_{\operatorname{dom}(g)}(z^{\ast})\cap\operatorname{\mathsf{NC}}_{\mathcal{S}}(z^{\ast})]^{\circ} 
\]

label: prop:EB1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:EB1}
Consider problem $\operatorname{HVI}({\mathsf{F}},g)$ with $\operatorname{dom}(g)$ a closed, convex, and nonempty subset of $\mathcal{Z}$. If $\mathcal{S}=\operatorname{zer}({\mathsf{F}}+\partial g)$ is weakly sharp, then 
$$
(\forall z\in\operatorname{dom}(g)):\quad \Theta(z\vert{\mathsf{F}},g,\operatorname{dom}(g))\geq \tau\operatorname{dist}(z,\mathcal{S}).
$$

title: Remark
body_md:
An important class of examples arises when $\rho=1$, notably in monotone linear complementarity problems in finite dimensions under nondegeneracy conditions \cite{burke1993weak,pang1997error}. In the case where the $\operatorname{HVI}({\mathsf{F}},g)$ reduces to a convex optimization problem, weak-sharpness implies an Hölderian errror bound, an assumption already imposed by \cite{Cabot2005} in the context of hierarchical minimization. Specifically, let us assume that ${\mathsf{F}}=0$ and $g\in\Gamma_{0}(\mathcal{Z})$. Then $\mathcal{S}=\operatorname*{argmin} g$, and acordingly, $H^{(0,g)}(z,z^{*})=g(z)-\min g$ for $z^{*}\in\mathcal{S}$. Hence, \eqref{eq:WSDef} implies 
    \[
    \frac{\kappa}{\rho}\operatorname{dist}(u,\operatorname*{argmin} g)^{\rho}\leq g(u)-\min g\qquad \forall u\in\mathcal{Z}.
    \]
If $\rho=1$, this is the weak-sharpness condition of \cite{burke1993weak}. The case $\rho=2$ corresponds to the "quadratic growth" condition of \cite{drusvyatskiy2018error}.\hfill{\footnotesize$\Diamond$}
